summary: amis-uni-area-widget ships webpack inline-loader that fetches and executes remote shell payload on consumer build hosts
details: The published widget entry dist/renderer.umd.js contains only `module.exports = require('./bsrc-loader.js!./payload.txt')`, abusing webpack's inline-loader `!` syntax so that any downstream project bundling this widget causes dist/bsrc-loader.js to run at build time. bsrc-loader.js first probes an internal Baidu SSRF endpoint (http://bsrc-ssrf.n.baidu-int.com) and, on Linux, spawns `/bin/sh -c` with a payload that curls/wgets http://49.232.169.67:80/slt and pipes the response into sh — arbitrary remote code execution on the builder host with an unpinned, opaque, attacker-controlled payload. The same loader base64url-encodes process.cwd(), the loader's rootContext/context/resourcePath, and the PID, and sends them as query parameters to http://49.232.169.67:80/bsrc-r270, leaking build-host paths and internal-network probe results over plain HTTP. The destination IP is assembled from a split octet array (['49','232','169','67'].join('.')) to evade literal-IP string matching, and the loader is presented under a cover-story name ('Authorized AI Suda webpack inline-loader validation').

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
